decisive_items: duodenal diverticula, wall thickening with mesenteric edema approximately 25 cm beyond the ligament of Treitz, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy with luminal patency
10-day history of worsening, intermittent epigastric pain, distention, and constipation
response.rationale: The CT findings of duodenal diverticula with wall thickening and mesenteric edema, along with fever and leukocytosis, are most consistent with acute diverticulitis. The resolution on follow-up CT supports an inflammatory process rather than malignancy or chronic IBD.

rejected.why: No evidence of mass, lymphadenopathy is reactive, and resolution on follow-up argues against lymphoma.
No eosinophilia, allergic history, or characteristic endoscopic findings; CT shows diverticula and localized inflammation.
CT shows luminal patency, ruling out obstruction; symptoms are not predominantly obstructive.
CT findings of diverticula and wall thickening are not typical for gastroenteritis, which usually lacks such localized inflammatory changes.
Mesenteric panniculitis would not explain duodenal diverticula and wall thickening; the inflammatory changes are centered on the diverticulum.
